moneyNote: User-approved fixed 140 SP per PC replaces the otherwise mandatory 4D6 × 10 SP roll. No dice were rolled during creation; equipment purchases use published list prices.

characters.name: Mara Holt
characters.loadout: Sword and large shield ready; bow slung. The bow needs both hands, so put the shield aside before wielding it. A ready large shield can use Shield Cover and Protector; a carried shield cannot.
characters.tactics: Stay adjacent to the companion most likely to need protection. Use the base Reaction for Protector when needed; your extra off-hand Reaction cannot fuel it. Climb with your kit and look for a secure rescue position before fighting. Shield Cover applies only while you are aware and the large shield is ready.

characters.name: Pebb Dallow
characters.loadout: Shortsword and small shield ready; light crossbow carried unloaded. The small shield can stay strapped to an arm while the crossbow is wielded, but cannot attack, Parry, or Active Guard until the crossbow is no longer wielded.
characters.tactics: Give negotiations room to work. Your heat sense cannot read a document or see through a wall: use a candle when light is needed. Open locks with Mechanisms and the Lock Picks' +1B; document work and a convincing explanation do not grant extra combat ability. Reloading the light crossbow spends Movement and the base Reaction.

characters.name: Dori Ashlar
characters.loadout: War hammer and medium shield ready; light crossbow carried unloaded. Put the shield aside before using the crossbow with two hands, or before handling a repair requiring both hands. Craft Tools are masonry tools.
characters.tactics: Inspect the load path before operating machinery. With connected stone underfoot, Earth Sense identifies approximate depth and instability, not hidden mechanisms or the answer to a puzzle. Block and Tackle needs your rope and gives +1B to Mechanisms involving large traps. Close-Quarters Knack removes only a penalty caused by confined space.

characters.name: Tamsin Reed

shaping.practice: Speak an audible litany while handling a washed section of the issued travelling rope. Preventing the speech or handling prevents casting; reserve a hand for the cord.
shaping.tell: Seven faint shadows gather around Tamsin and the affected subject or area. Anyone watching the Practice notices it; automatic notice extends 10 × Magnitude metres from the Shaper and ranged target/area, minimum 3 m.

examples.name: Close the wound
examples.effect: Touch one willing living subject: restore 1D4 HP once, up to maximum; remove Bleeding and Dying. This does not count as Surgery or remove Wounded. No defence.

examples.name: Reach the casualty
examples.effect: One willing living subject within 15 m and an unobstructed route: restore 2D4 HP once, capped at maximum; remove Bleeding and Dying. This is not Surgery. No defence.

examples.name: Mend the major wound
examples.effect: Touch one willing living subject: restore 3D4 HP once, capped at maximum, remove Bleeding and Dying, and count as Surgery to unlock normal recovery. Wounded ends only once HP exceeds MWL. No defence.

examples.name: Read the injury
examples.effect: Touch one willing subject and diagnose one present bodily injury from evidence in the body. This is one answer, not continuous monitoring; it restores no HP and grants no free Healing bonus. No defence.

characters.loadout: Mace and medium shield ready; sling stowed. Put the mace away to handle the prayer cord; put both items away when treatment needs both hands. Ordinary treatment needs a Healing Kit and spends a use even when it fails.
characters.tactics: Use ordinary Healing when appropriate and save PP for time-critical care. Battlefield treatment spends the entire round, including Movement and all Reactions, while you and the patient remain stationary. Casting normally spends only the Combat Action, provided Practice is possible. Keep at least 1 PP if you need to remain conscious.

characters.name: Ilen Sedge
characters.loadout: Longbow held ready, with no arrow nocked; shortsword sheathed, small shield strapped. While the two-handed bow is wielded, the strapped shield cannot attack, Parry, or Active Guard. Nocking an arrow uses the normal Ready option.
characters.tactics: Report danger before running into it. Quick Reflexes is already included in Combat Order. Aim can help a clear shot; Steady Aim retains that benefit through a Reaction, but not loss of sight or postponing the shot beyond your next Combat Action. Battle Awareness prevents the flanking/rear bonus only while you are aware of at least one enemy.

characters.name: Orren Pike
characters.loadout: Great hammer ready in both hands; two javelins carried, one from the free package and one purchased. A two-handed hammer gives no off-hand option. Put it aside before grappling.
characters.tactics: Ask whether the aim is rescue, capture, or lethal force. Start a grapple through the ordinary rules before using Wrestler. Subdue can use your blunt great hammer or unarmed attack; it is a special attack, not automatic harmless damage. Your strong DM also applies to thrown javelins, but your Ranged Combat is untrained.

characters.name: Seris Vale
characters.loadout: Longbow held ready, with no arrow nocked; longspear carried. Each needs two hands and offers no off-hand option. A dagger and a free hand can provide the normal one-handed option after changing equipment.
characters.tactics: Use Natural Lore for tracking, weather, navigation, and survival, and Perception to notice immediate danger. Terrain Expertise and Tracker can both remove remaining penalties from a forest tracking test but never create Bonus dice. Low-Light Sight improves dim light, not pitch black or fog. You are a guide, not an automatically successful scout.

characters.name: Nerin Quill

shaping.practice: Speak a measured count while tracing two intersecting lines with a free hand. Preventing speech or the gesture prevents casting.
shaping.tell: Straight edges double around Nerin and the affected subject or area. Anyone watching the Practice notices it; automatic notice extends 10 × Magnitude metres from the Shaper and ranged target/area, minimum 3 m.

examples.name: Measured shove
examples.effect: Move one human-sized subject within 15 m up to 3 m along a clear route. An unwilling subject opposes with Resilience, spending no Reaction. This buys movement once, not damage, prone, restraint, or continuing control; actual environmental consequences still use their normal rules.

examples.name: Hold to the wall
examples.effect: Self or one willing touched subject gains the ability to climb ordinary vertical stone by force-supported footing for a scene or 10 minutes. Use normal Movement; difficult conditions can still require Athletics. The subject directs their own movement, so this needs no maintenance Action. Ongoing M3; no extra movement Action or protection from falling damage.

examples.name: Force bolt
examples.effect: Projected Harm to one target within 15 m along an unobstructed route: 2D6 HP damage once; no DM. Cover and nonmagical AP apply. The target may oppose with Dodge or ready-shield Active Guard at -1P. Its Impact Size is Medium. No free push, prone, or repeat damage.

examples.name: Distant force bolt
examples.effect: The same Projected Harm at up to 50 m: 2D6 HP damage, Medium impact, normal cover/AP and opposed Dodge or shield Active Guard at -1P. M4 overreaches by one, so the casting takes -1P and a failed casting causes Backlash. No DM or free movement.

characters.loadout: Shortsword ready with the other hand free for Practice; small shield carried. Ready the shield when needed, but put an item away again before casting. The free hand already counts for ordinary off-hand options.
characters.tactics: Explain the whole intended effect before casting. Your two exact cells provide force control and force harm, not healing, wards, teleportation, or all magic. Force bolts use Shaping rather than Ranged Combat. If PP are low, support a companion with ordinary skills or withdraw; 0 PP means unconsciousness.
